newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS -Dlr vols firm as spot glimpses 1.80 marks.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS -Dlr vols firm as spot glimpses 1.80 marks.

text.p: Implied volatilities in dollar/mark options firmed as choppiness prevailed in spot following recent sharp moves -- mostly downwards -- which briefly brought the key 1.8000 level into sight today.

With fluctuations in the spot market and speculation swirling about the possibility of the Bundesbank boosting rates by shifting to variable-rate money market tenders, it was difficult to sell off dollar/mark volatilities now, traders said.

"There was quite a downward correction in dollar/mark on Friday which drove volatilities higher, and vols have stayed there ever since," said an options trader at a Japanese bank in London. "And there are plenty of factors this week, like the Bundesbank meeting and the FOMC."

One-month dollar/mark vols were quoted at 11.45/80 percent at 1150 GMT against their late Friday European level of 10.90/30. Spot dollar/mark, after falling to its lowest in nearly a month at 1.8060 earlier, had recovered to 1.8168/73 against Friday's 1.8210/20.

The slide in the spot rate had shifted the market's preference just slightly in favour of mark calls. Dollar/mark 25-delta risk reversals were skewed towards mark calls at -0.05/0.2 against around par late on Friday.

Traders said they did not expect volatilities to ease much in the run-up to the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) policy-making meeting on Tuesday, and the Bundesbank's council meeting, its first after a four-week break, on Thursday.

"Any strong signal (from the FOMC or the Bundesbank) and the spot market could bolt in one direction, in which case vols would spring up. But it's difficult to do anything now," the Japanese bank trader said.
Dollar/yen volatilities were also firm after spot market fluctuations of two to three yen per day in the latter half of last week, traders said.
One-month vols were quoted at 12.40/60 percent compared with 12.20/50 in late Friday trade. Spot dollar/yen was at 117.76/86, off its session high of 118.00, against 117.48/58 on Friday.
Demand was still biased towards dollar calls because at spot dollar/yen's current levels, an upside target of 120 was still within reach, traders said.
Risk reversals showed a preference for dollar calls at 0.2/0.5 against Friday's 0.3/0.6.

"The point to note about dollar/yen vols right now is that there is a lot of interest in buying the back end of dollar/yen, so the longer end is staying very firm," said a trader at a Canadian bank here.
The dollar/yen vols curve was virtually flat, with one-year vols at the far end nearly equalling one-month at 12.35/45 percent against Friday's 12.30/60.
Mark/yen vols stayed firm as spot continued its strong rebound from 25-month lows hit last week. One-month vols were at 11.70/12.20 against Friday's 11.50/80.
Meanwhile, traders noted little movement in sterling vols, as the market's eyes were fixed elsewhere while spot sterling/mark and cable stayed within familiar ranges above 2.90 marks and $1.60.
One-month sterling/mark vols were at 11.80/12.30 percent against Friday's 11.60/12.00, while cable vols were at 10.10/40 against 10.00/40.
